Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a dense consolidation in the right upper lobe that is sharply demarcated inferiorly by the horizontal fissure, indicating it respects the anatomical boundaries of the lobe. This pattern, often accompanied by air bronchograms (visible air-filled bronchi within the opaque lung), is the classic radiographic presentation of lobar pneumonia caused by an infectious process.
